title: Cheese and Onion Pasty
subtitle: Shortcrust pastry filled with potato, cheese, and onion
excerpt: A vegetarian Cornish-style pasty with a filling of raw potato, onion, and sharp cheddar, all sealed in a short, buttery pastry and baked until golden. Better than the meat version for many who make it.

recipe.sourceNotes: The Cornish pasty is a protected geographical indication dish from Cornwall, traditionally filled with beef skirt, swede, potato, and onion. The cheese and onion variant is one of the most popular pasty fillings elsewhere in Britain and is the standard vegetarian alternative. The key technique from the traditional Cornish version is used here: the filling goes in raw, not pre-cooked, and cooks inside the sealed pastry. This keeps the filling moist and the potato from becoming mushy.

content.text: The filling goes in raw: thin slices of potato and onion with grated cheese, seasoned well. Raw potato inside the sealed pastry steams in its own moisture and cooks through in 50 minutes at a high temperature. Slice the potato no thicker than 3 mm or the centre will still be hard when the pastry is done. Crimp the pastry firmly on top so it does not open in the oven.
Make the pastry: rub the cold butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Add the water and bring together into a firm dough. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Mix the potato slices, onion, and grated cheddar together. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Divide the dough into 4 pieces. Roll each to a circle about 22 cm across. Place a quarter of the filling on one half of each circle, leaving a 2 cm border. Fold the pastry over the filling. Press the edges firmly together and crimp to seal.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Put the pasties on a lined baking tray. Brush with beaten egg and cut two small slits in the top of each. Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 10 minutes before eating; the filling is very hot inside.
